newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Taleban plane lands at Afghan government airbase.
newsitem.headline: Taleban plane lands at Afghan government airbase.

text.p: A transport plane of the rebel Taleban militia landed at an Afghan government military airbase on Tuesday, Kabul radio and Taleban sources said.
Government-controlled Kabul radio said an M-32 transport plane had been hijacked by a "brave mujahid (struggler)" during a flight between the Taleban-held cities of Herat and Kandahar.
The radio, monitored in Islamabad, said the plane was carrying 33 Taleban members and seven Pakistani nationals when it landed at Bagram airbase 50 km (31 miles) north of Kabul.
Taleban sources confirmed that the plane had landed in Bagram, but said the pilot had defected. They denied that any Pakistanis were on board the aircraft.
No independent account of the incident was available.
The Afghan government accuses Pakistan of supporting the Taleban, fighting to oust President Burhanuddin Rabbani and install a strict Islamic order. Islamabad denies the charge.
